newsitem.title: QATAR: SQUASH-JANSHER STRUGGLES BEFORE REACHING QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER STRUGGLES BEFORE REACHING QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Seven times world champion Jansher Khan endured a marathon struggle before reaching the quarter-finals of the Qatar International on Monday, and then launched an angry attack on opponent Ahmed Barada of Egypt.
Jansher beat Barada 15-10 15-13 14-15 8-15 15-9 in a one and a half hour match, but then criticised his rival's tactics.
"I've played him three times now and there's always a problem with him because he blocks me a lot," said the Pakistani who is bidding to win the title for a fifth consecutive year.

"If Barada played a clean game, then I would say he's a good player. But I can't because he is always pushing and shoving. He will have to change for the future," he said. Jansher also criticised the referee for not taking action.
Jansher could have wrapped up the match in three games. He had match ball at 14-14 in the third game, but a winning shot was called a let and Barada won the game 15-14 with a drop volley.
The decision caused Jansher to lose concentration in the fourth game which the 20-year-old Egyptian won to take the match into a deciding fifth game.
Jansher regained his composure in the fifth game and never looked in serious trouble again as errors crept back into Barada's game.
Earlier, Peter Nicol of Scotland, seeded fourth, was beaten by France's Julien Bonetat. World 17th ranked Bonetat won 15-12 15-13 15-8.
